text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

Just days before the release of the Wallis inquiry into the financial system, Federal Treasurer Peter Costello has issued a strong warning to the big banks and life offices not to embark on major take-overs or mergers before the Federal Government responded to the long-awaited inquiry, saying if they do so it is at their own risk. Page 1.

After the group posted a 70 per cent increase in third-quarter profit to A$378 million but managed only a 6.3 per cent rise in net profit to A$1.17 billion for the nine months to February 28, BHP managing director John Prescott Told Channel Nine's Busines Sunday program yesterday the Big Australian's steel and copper arms needed to make major improvements. Page 23.

Speaking on Channel Nine's Business Sunday program yesterday, BHP managing director John Prescott revealed the company had been reviewing its 37 per cent investment in Foster's Brewing Group and was initiating its own inquiries for a sale after receiving resh approaches about the stake in the past few weeks. Page 23.

In a major step towards a deal that will rationalise the whole pay-TV and telco industry, American telco US West has joined Kerry Stokes's Seven Network and Kerry Packer's PBL in agreeing to sell its shares in the Optus Vision cable-TV network
to Optus Comunications, a move which gives Optus 100 per cent control of Vision. Page 25.

Village Roadshow group general manager Peter Foo said yesterday Austereo faced a large drop in profit in 1996-97 as the expiration of an earnings guarantee from Village coincided with the radio network facing a tax bill for the first time in two years, an he said Village's bid for Austereo was aimed at offsetting the expected huge slump in earnings. Page 25.

Highlands Pacific Ltd chairman Lou Clinton said yesterday that the continuing political unrest in Papua New Guinea was of concern to international investors, but would not harm his company's upcoming A$190 million float, which would proceed on schedule. Pge 25.
THE AUSTRALIAN

Sources close to the Wallis inquiry into the financial system, headed by leading industrialist Stan Wallis, have signalled a series of major changes to the financial services system aimed at boosting competition and lowering the cost of
financial services- a move which would see non-bank financial institutions emerge as big winners. Page 17.

In a wide-ranging interview yesterday, BHP managing director John Prescott said that maintaining the group's 85-year-old integrated steelmaking operation in Newcastle could prove 'unsustainable' and acknowledged market expectations that BHP Steel would ony retain the rod and bar rolls at the plant. Page 17.

BHP chief executive John Prescott has revealed he is unhappy with the GDP growth rates of between 4 per cent and 4.5 per cent canvassed recently by Prime Minister John Howard, saying the Federal Government is ignoring Australia's economic growth potentialin favour of "academic debates about economic theory". Page 17.

Ahead of an expected and dreaded United States interest rate increase, the outcome of the ACTU's living wage claim, which is before the Industrial Relations Commission, and the imminent outcome of the Wallis inquiry into the financial system, financial makets are commencing the week on an uncertain note. Page 17.

In what would be a settlement of a long-running legal dispute with minority Optus Vision shareholder the Seven Network Ltd, Optus Communications is expected to give details early today of a plan that will result in a rearrangement of Optus' pay TV interess as the group assumes full control of Vision, its half-owned pay-TV arm. Page 19.

Speaking at an Institute of Chartered Accountants function in Melbourne on Friday, entrepreneur John Elliott made an unorthodox assessment of the Australian economy, drawing a link between low inflation and the slow pace of new job creation claiming low iflation means "low employment". Page 19.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

The four stockbroking firms that underwrote the unsuccessful Stadium Australia float - which is raising money to build the Olympic stadium - look set to pick up a shortfall of A$240 million worth of unsold Stadium memberships when the raising
closes on Thrsday. Page 37.

After St George Bank chairman Frank Conroy said yesterday he knew some investment banks had approached institutional investors about an issue, the Bank's board will meet today to decide on the future of its proposed A$360 million capital raising, with several investment banks, including Merrill Lynch, CS First Boston and Bankers Trust, rumoured to be interested. Page 37.

Speaking on Channel Nine's Business Sunday program yesterday, RTZ-CRA chief executive Leon Davis said the uncertainty created by the High Court's controversial Wik ruling had not affected its investment choices, saying RTZ-CRA, one of the world's largest esources companies, had not been holding back from investing in Australia while indigenous title was clarified. Page 37.

Speaking on Channel Nine's Business Sunday program yesterday, BHP managing director John Prescott confirmed ongoing stockmarket rumours that the resources giant is now prepared to quit its 37 per cent stake in Foster's Brewing Group, saying the group was actively looking" at new ways of capturing value from the investment. Page 39.

Despite a rumoured settlement in the ongoing legal battle between the Optus Vision shareholders and Seven Network having been agreed upon, talks aimed at restructuring pay-TV and local telephony group Optus Vision are expected to go past today's
deadline,despite an all-weekend effort to settle the issue. Page 39.

Aussie Home Loans has taken a risky step by introducing a 95 per cent loan-to-valuation ratio for all buyers of new homes - a first among major mortgage lenders, who usually operate on a ratio of 80 per cent. The move by Aussie Home Loans will increase th possibility of loan defaults, but place pressure on other lenders. Page 39.
THE AGE

As part of the Federal Government's package for small business owners, a fund of hundreds of millions of dollars will be established to firms who meet certain criteria. The fund is part of the Government's pledge to cut red tape to boost jobs, and will alo assist in an easing of the fringe-benefits tax. Page B1.

BHP's managing director John Prescott has indicated that the company may sell its 37 per cent stake in Foster's Brewing Group in a deal worth A$1.8 billion. The leading prospect to buy the stock is Canada's Molson Group, with Heineken, Phillip Morris
and Miller Brewing also expressing interest. Page B1.

Woodside Petroleum chairman John Akehurst has predicted that the company, valued at A$6 billion, will double in size over the next five to seven years. This would be additional to a similar expansion rate over the past three years. Woodside currently provdes shareholders with a return of less than the industry average. Page B1.

The sharemarket closes this week on the float of the new Olympic stadium, Stadium Australia. The four underwriters will be obliged to buy up to A$240 million of unsold Stadium memberships after a public response which was far less enthusiastic than expectd. Page B1.

Two applicants in a legal challenge to landowner agreements over Ross Mining's Golden Ridge gold project have withdrawn from the case, claiming that authorisation to commence proceedings was not provided. Page B3.

The Australian Chamber of Manufacturers has claimed that Government cuts in export development programs have halted the growth of manufactured exports, threatened Budget targets and future employment prospects. Page B3.
-- Sydney newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
